## Understand the request before writing

Read the actual requirements, current round and relevant implementation. Same behavior under the same conditions is a duplicate; refer to the existing requirement. A new requirement selected for the current MVP returns to step1 and updates that same plan, retaining valid work. Review all ten steps for changed meaning; do not blindly replay them. If Future reveals an irreversible current decision, show the evidence and smallest necessary current correction for Human decision before authoring it. For an actual bug, reproduce violation of the approved requirement and identify the observed running source, configuration and artifact, separately from the intended release. PAUSED, CANCELLED and UNKNOWN observations are not running-state success. Select master only when it is a suitable maintenance baseline; otherwise identify the verified production commit and an explicitly authorized maintenance branch. Preserve earlier fixes, test the candidate and combined version under G2, and record each fix's disposition on master. Git operations and release still require their own scope. Interrupting an independent feature requires retaining its current checkpoint and an explicit Human priority decision; only one implementation remains active.

## Three maps and semantic review

The document map contains scoped IDs/links and purposes; the implementation map contains actual files/symbols and derived relations; the responsibility mapping relates requirements and implementation many-to-many, including tests. Keep the authored mapping at the project-selected path (default `docs/architecture/traceability.md`); generate reverse lookup from it. Do not create a fourth test map or duplicate progress table.

Read-only adapter modules `maps.mjs`, `maps-web.mjs`, and `maps-cpp.mjs` expose evidence-producing APIs for a trusted integration runner. They do not select or execute a compiler. The C++ adapter consumes the bounded runner's Clang JSON receipt with input basis, target/configuration, tool identity and diagnostics. The Web adapter receives trusted preloaded TypeScript/Svelte capabilities, never project-selected executable config. Using an integration runner/compiler requires the established tool/environment grant; absence of that capability is a blocker, not permission to emulate it. Raw AST/lexical candidates cannot prove all runtime dispatch. Record generated-file, alias, dynamic URL, callback, virtual, event, shared-data and resource limitations.

Manually inspect supported and unsupported relations against real source. Add event/config/data/operation consumers with exact evidence and a reason, not a guessed relationship name. Confirm assertion meaning: a test that merely calls a function is not proof of the requirement. Incorrect behavior under a mutant must be distinguishable by the relevant assertion. A missing adapter or stale/incomplete receipt does not establish an empty dependency graph.

## Trusted request and persistent plan

READ requires `permission: {root, readProject: true, allowReadLocalGit: boolean}`. Existing Git requires local read permission; no fetch occurs. Optional `requiredFiles` are `{path, anchor}` references, with null anchor when absent. The returned `basis`, `inputBasis`, project/current item and checkout describe this exact read, not execution authority. Add required evidence before reading the basis. Never refresh an unexpected identity silently.

For OPEN, first READ with `graph` containing `format: 'kidea-impact-graph-r1'`, nonempty `nodes` and `seeds`, `edges`, and `diagnostics`. Each node has stable `id`, `name`, `scopeRef`, `completionRef`, nonempty `inputRefs`. Each edge points from changed producer to potentially affected consumer, with `from`, `to`, a substantive `reason` and nonempty `evidenceRefs`. This is a reviewed consequence graph, not an unexamined raw call graph. Include all relevant consumers; mark unresolved scope in diagnostics. A cycle is legal here; task dependency cycles remain forbidden.

Mutating requests include the exact returned `expectedBasis`, `expectedProjectId`, `expectedRoundId`, `expectedOwnerId`, `expectedGit` (full checkout object or null). OPEN creates one schema2 plan, one Item per affected node and a return point for the original work. The plan is authoritative; map/assessment JSON artifacts are immutable evidence linked from Item refs, not another queue. REFRESH conservatively reopens affected conclusions when source/config/tool basis changed. Even a NO_CHANGE verdict propagates to consumers. A stable ID, empty diff, exhausted edge traversal or quota does not close an obligation.

REPLAN updates this same plan after scope review. READ with the proposed graph and `replacement: {reason,evidenceRefs,dispositions}`; each prior Item needs a disposition `{itemId,verdict:'REASSESS'|'RETIRED_FROM_SCOPE',reason}`. Mutating permission additionally requires `allowImpactReplan:true`. Existing result evidence is retained for surviving IDs, but every revised obligation is reevaluated. Review stale approvals through approve first; REPLAN does not preserve approval by fiat. Do not recreate a missing file or infer semantic identity from its new filename.

NEEDS_CHANGE requires actual authorized changes/checks before `resolved:true`; prose or this helper does not perform them. UNKNOWN remains unresolved. The helper binds source versions and retains each assessment. All claims/evidence remain subject to content review.

CLOSE requires all current obligations resolved, no graph diagnostic/blocker, current source versions and approved gates for every impact item. Review packages must cover each item's current inputs, scope/completion and latest assessment; an unrelated approval does not suffice. Include `closure: {conditionsMet:true,semanticStatement,evidenceRefs}` from the actual gate review. CLOSE restores the original continuation point; it does not mark the product round DONE, approve R06 or authorize release.

## Resume and interruption

Resume READ includes recorded impact obligations and source-version freshness. Read change context to check the complete tool/graph basis before evaluating or closing. Missing rule/Git object, conflict, wrong root, stale review or pending marker blocks dependent writes. Never remove a marker or replay its recorded commands. READ/SAVE retain their old authority: neither automatically advances impact work.

An unstable graph or repeated unchanged conclusion remains unresolved. The approved R06 fixture uses three unchanged transitions or twenty evaluations as canaries; these numbers are not product graph limits. Follow the existing host/runtime and single-cooperative-run constraints.

## Read and continue

Construct `{operation: 'READ', permission: {root, readProject: true, allowReadLocalGit}, requiredFiles: []}` in memory from the current permission. Use the exact selected root; do not scan ancestors or select a different checkout. `allowReadLocalGit` is an explicit boolean. An existing Git checkout requires that permission to inspect its local HEAD, branch and unmerged entries. Nothing fetches, pulls, switches branches, commits or changes the index. The helper reads the indexed graph and returns the current item, parents, transitive dependencies, return stack, relevant blockers, recorded reviews, operation observations and source paths/digests. Add required local scripts/config/rule files as `requiredFiles: [{path, anchor}]`, with null anchor if absent. This verifies file/anchor presence, not that a tool is installed or a command is correct. Do not read secrets or unrelated files merely to populate context.

Read the actual relevant product documents and controlling dependencies in full. The returned paths, hashes and task summary do not replace semantic analysis. Determine what was done, what remains, which review is current, and whether permission, toolchain, environment and required checks are still sufficient. A recorded APPROVED label is not authenticated Human intent, and matching bytes do not establish complete dependency coverage.

Report briefly where work stands, then continue only the current permitted work through capabilities already implemented: discussion/clarification, supported read checks, explicit review operations and saving context. Do not stop just to demand another Kidea command for ordinary Human feedback. Conversely, if the next step requires an unavailable product executor, task/decomposition transition, environment access or additional permission, state that specific limit. Do not simulate a missing feature through internal writer calls or arbitrary shell writes.

CONTEXT_READY means the structural context was bound, **not permission to execute**. WAITING retains valid context plus relevant recorded blockers/dependencies or an already-DONE current item; resolve the issue through permitted discussion/actions, not by clearing labels, rerunning completed work or choosing a new item. # Business scope, rules and test specifications

Use this method when clarifying or reviewing business content in the selected permitted scope. It does not grant product writes, new actions, task transitions, approval or execution. The public helper limitations in SKILL.md still apply. A separately authorized authoring exercise is not helper-driven product execution.

## Scope and a useful slice

Read the established Feature Map, relevant decisions and actual source documents, not only their labels/hashes. For an existing product distinguish observed implementation from desired behavior; do not redefine requirements to fit code. Keep the original Human request or its source reference separate from interpretation.

Establish who uses the product, the result they need, included/excluded behavior, public/private data, permissions and material platform/operational constraints. Keep MVP/Future/Idea as Human-selected categories; uncertainty is not selection. Ask whether A/B is relevant, but do not add experiments by default or specify Future deeply. Batch all currently identifiable material decisions, execution permissions and verification limits in one understandable package with short examples. After approval perform the covered work continuously; ask again only for a genuinely new decision, conflict, permission or limit. Approval of a plan is not approval of its unseen outputs.

Find shared responsibilities from actual callers, owned state, invariants and input/output contracts; matching names alone do not justify merging. Prefer keeping single-use behavior in its Feature unless a state invariant genuinely crosses boundaries. Propose a small user-result slice with the shared dependencies needed to describe it correctly, including downstream change obligations. Human approval of the boundaries/slice may be batched with scope when ready; it does not approve unwritten rules. Do not wait for every future shared area to be specified before an independent slice.

Use the project's existing source layout. An index holds IDs/descriptions/links, not a second current-task/approval tracker. Product rules remain in product documents; supported review/context records retain workflow evidence. Do not impose a directory/file for every rule or invent a new schema.

## Make behavior decidable

For new content describe actor/trigger/purpose, input and output meanings and valid domains, units/precision/null/absent handling when relevant. Describe condition → observable result and changed/unchanged state, invalid cases and invariants. Stateful behavior needs a before/event/condition/after table and a responsible authority. Stateless behavior does not need artificial state.

Read reused contracts fully and link the exact section rather than copying a second rule. A flow table is the source for branches, results and next step/end, linking rules without restating them. A diagram, if useful, is derived from that table. If combined invalid conditions affect the observable result, establish precedence instead of inventing it; do not universalize one flow's first-error order.
